findings.fact: Prior to award, the Bidder must be registered in the New York State Vendor File, and if not already registered, must request assignment of a Vendor ID from DTF.
findings.business_implication: Without registration, the bidder cannot be awarded the contract, even if the bid is otherwise successful. This is a mandatory administrative step.
findings.action_recommendation: Check if your company is already registered in the NYS Vendor File. If not, complete the OSC Substitute W-9 Form and submit it to DTF as soon as possible to obtain a Vendor ID.

findings.business_implication: Violating the lobbying restrictions can lead to rejection of the bid or debarment. The bidder must ensure all communications go through the designated contact and that required forms are submitted.

findings.business_implication: Failure to disclose such determinations can result in disqualification. The bidder must be transparent about any past issues to avoid penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Check if your company has any prior non-responsibility determinations in the last four years. If so, disclose them accurately in Attachment 3 and be prepared to explain the circumstances.

findings.title: Pricing Requirements
findings.fact: Prices are to be provided by the Bidder on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form. A Bidder’s failure to provide a complete pricing response will result in the Bidder’s proposal being deemed non-responsive. Bidders must not modify or change the Attachment. Any pricing information or add-on costs that do not conform to the presentation allowed on Attachment 1 cannot be evaluated, will be disregarded as extraneous, and cannot be charged to the Department. Charges for travel cannot be listed as separate line items on the bid response form. The prices bid for each item must be inclusive of all costs. Prices as they appear on submitted bids must be guaranteed by the vendor for the term of the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all costs are fully loaded into the pricing on Attachment 1, with no separate charges for travel or other add-ons. Any incomplete or non-compliant pricing will result in disqualification. The prices must remain fixed for the entire contract term, so the bidder must accurately estimate costs and avoid underpricing.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review Attachment 1 and ensure all required pricing fields are completed accurately. Include all costs (e.g., labor, travel, materials) in the unit prices. Do not modify the form. Verify that the total price is competitive and sustainable for the contract duration.

quotes.quote: 6. PRICE Prices are to be provided by the Bidder on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form. Any pricing information or add-on costs that do not conform to the presentation allowed on Attachment 1 cannot be evaluated, will be disregarded as extraneous, and cannot be charged to the Department. Charges for travel cannot be listed as separate line items on the bid response form. The prices bid for each item must be inclusive of all costs. Prices as they appear on submitted bids must be guaranteed by the vendor for the term of the Agreement.

findings.title: Payment Terms
findings.fact: Payment for invoices submitted by the awarded Bidder shall only be rendered electronically unless payment by paper check is expressly authorized by the Commissioner, at the Commissioner’s sole discretion, due to extenuating circumstances. The awarded Bidder shall comply with the State Comptroller’s procedures to authorize electronic payments. Invoices cannot reflect charges in excess of the totals bid on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, unless the additionally incurred costs are mutually agreed upon in writing between the Bidder and an authorized Department representative. The Department will not pay any costs associated with goods or services that have not been received. Payment will be made only upon submission of proper invoices by the awarded Bidder, and in accordance with Article 11-A of New York State Finance Law.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be set up to receive electronic payments through the State Comptroller's system. Failure to comply may result in non-payment. Invoices must match the bid amounts exactly, and any additional costs require prior written approval. The Department will only pay for goods/services actually received, so the bidder must ensure proper delivery and documentation.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the company is registered for electronic payments with the NYS Comptroller's office. Familiarize with the invoicing requirements, including the need for a valid PO number and line item details. Establish internal processes to prevent invoicing errors and to obtain written approval for any extra costs before incurring them.

quotes.quote: 7. FEES AND PAYMENT Electronic Payment Payment for invoices submitted by the awarded Bidder shall only be rendered electronically unless payment by paper check is expressly authorized by the Commissioner, at the Commissioner’s sole discretion, due to extenuating circumstances. Such electronic payment shall be made in accordance with ordinary State procedures and practices. The awarded Bidder shall comply with the State Comptroller’s procedures to authorize electronic payments. Authorization forms are available at the State Comptroller’s website at www.osc.state.ny.us/epay/index.htm, by email at helpdesk@sfs.ny.gov, or by telephone at (855)-233-8363. The Bidder acknowledges that it will not receive payment on any invoices submitted under this Agreement if it does not comply with the State Comptroller’s electronic procedures, except where the Commissioner has expressly authorized payment by paper check as set forth above. Invoices cannot reflect charges in excess of the totals bid on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, unless the additionally incurred costs are mutually agreed upon in writing between the Bidder and an authorized Department representative. The Department will not pay any costs associated with goods or services that have not been received. Properly Submitted Invoices Payment will be made only upon submission of proper invoices by the awarded Bidder, and in accordance with Article 11-A of New York State Finance Law.

findings.title: Method of Award
findings.fact: The award will be made to the responsive and responsible Bidder who provides the lowest overall cost and meets all requirements set forth in this RFQ. The total cost will be calculated using the information provided on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form. In the event tie bids are received by the Department, the earliest bid received shall determine the winner.
findings.business_implication: The contract will be awarded based on the lowest total cost, so the bidder must offer a competitive price while meeting all technical requirements. Since tie bids are decided by earliest submission, submitting early could be advantageous.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a pricing strategy that is competitive but also covers all costs. Ensure all requirements are met to be considered responsive. Submit the bid as early as possible to gain an advantage in case of a tie.

quotes.quote: 8. METHOD OF AWARD The award will be made to the responsive and responsible Bidder who provides the lowest overall cost and meets all requirements set forth in this RFQ. findings.title: Installation Costs
findings.fact: All installation costs must be provided on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, and must be inclusive of all labor and travel to the Department’s three (3) locations. The cost must include any additional items required for proper installation (i.e., cables, zip ties, harnesses).
findings.business_implication: The bidder must accurately estimate installation costs for three locations, including all labor, travel, and materials. These costs must be included in the pricing on Attachment 1, with no separate charges. Underestimating could lead to financial loss, while overestimating may make the bid less competitive.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough assessment of the installation requirements at each location. Prepare a detailed cost breakdown, including travel time, labor hours, and materials. Ensure all costs are incorporated into the Attachment 1 pricing. Consider potential contingencies to avoid underpricing.

quotes.quote: All installation costs must be provided on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, and must be inclusive of all labor and travel to the Department’s three (3) locations. The cost must include any additional items required for proper installation (i.e., cables, zip ties, harnesses).

findings.title: Ongoing Support and Maintenance Costs
findings.fact: If any devices are identified by the Department to require maintenance or replacement, not resulting from the negligence of any DTF employee, the devices and/or services must be provided to the Department at no cost within 30 days of the Department’s notification.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is obligated to provide maintenance and replacement at no cost for the entire contract term, except for damage caused by the Department's negligence. This could result in significant financial exposure if devices fail or become obsolete. The bidder must factor in these potential costs when pricing the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the reliability and expected lifespan of the proposed hardware. Include a contingency in the pricing to cover potential no-cost replacements. findings.title: Ambiguity in hardware installation method
findings.fact: The hardware requirements state that devices must be installed via the vehicle's engine diagnostics port and not require being hard wired directly to the vehicle's battery, but the installation services requirements mention that the cost must include any additional items required for proper installation (i.e., cables, zip ties, harnesses), which could imply hard wiring might be needed.
findings.business_implication: There is a potential contradiction: the hardware must not require hard wiring, but installation costs may include items typically used for hard wiring. This ambiguity could lead to disputes over installation methods and costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from DTF on whether hard wiring is permitted or required. Ensure the proposed solution strictly complies with the 'no hard wiring' requirement and clarify the scope of 'additional items' in the quote.

quotes.quote: Be installed via the vehicle’s engine diagnostics port and not require being hard wired directly to the vehicle’s battery;
The cost must include any additional items required for proper installation (i.e., cables, zip ties, harnesses).

findings.title: Ambiguity in software data storage requirement
findings.fact: The software requirements state that the software must have the capability to store information when network coverage is unavailable and transmit that information once network coverage is regained, but the note says 'Complete and accurate data must be made available to DTF staff whether within network coverage or outside of network coverage.' This could be interpreted as requiring real-time availability even without network, which may conflict with the store-and-forward capability.
findings.business_implication: The requirement for data availability outside network coverage could be interpreted as needing real-time access, which may not be feasible with store-and-forward. This ambiguity could lead to performance expectations that are difficult to meet.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with DTF whether 'made available' means real-time access or if store-and-forward is acceptable. Propose a solution that ensures data is accessible as soon as connectivity is restored, and document this interpretation in the proposal.

quotes.quote: Have the capability to store information when network coverage is unavailable and transmit that information once network coverage is regained;
Note: Complete and accurate data must be made available to DTF staff whether within network coverage or outside of network coverage.
